title: J. I. de Swart (St Petersburg) to P. van Bleiswijk, 8 March 1782, Nationaal Archief 3.01.25 inv. 610 (DECODE R1036)

documents.shelfmark: Nationaal Archief 3.01.25 (P. van Bleiswijk) inv. 610; DECODE R1036

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the record; no edition found. The key survives separately as the 1765 Croiset codebook, DECODE R1038.

transcription.source: DECODE's authenticated manual transcription of the ciphertext, checked against the nine scans
transcription.notes: Two leaves are duplicate copies (images 5419/5421, 5420/5422). Their token sequences agree 96.7% and 99.6% and were merged, preferring readings present in the key. Marks on single digits are kept as part of the group.

plaintext.source: No decipherment found. Leeuw (2000) notes that two codebooks were used.

transcription.notes: The first 1,928 groups use a different, missing key. The switch is at group 180 of image 5459. 1,928 groups in the first (missing) code, images 5453-5458 and the first 179 groups of 5459; 5,956 in the 1765 key, group 180 of 5459 to 5474

system.summary: Three-digit Dutch code-nomenclator (Croiset 1765, Russia legation) with words, syllables and letters; a mark on one digit makes a separate group.
system.notes: Five digit marks (two strokes, underline, caret, circle, barred circle). Collapsing them to the base number creates false homographs.

prior_solution.where: No published decipherment of R1036 or R1040 was found; the key R1038 is on DECODE

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched R1036, R1040 and R1038 scans and DECODE transcriptions, plus sibling pairs R2045, R2195, R2032, R2051 and R2052.
Leeuw 2000 and the Oterleek-codes paper (HistoCrypt 2026) identified the Croiset codebook family and the two-codebook 1787 letter. No prior decipherment was found.
Parsed DECODE's R1038 key transcription to 5,961 entries, keeping the digit marks as part of the group.
Tried the 1803 Croiset relative on R1036/R1040. The apparent hits gave nonsense.
Applied the key to R1036: 1,448 of 1,719 groups (84.2%). Then 25 values from repeated contexts (Spa+nje, Dene+mar+ken, lijk, ing[en]) brought it to 91.9%.
Located the codebook switch in R1040 at group 180 of image 5459 and read the second segment with the 1765 key at 84-90% a page.
Aligned the 1784-86 plain/cipher pairs R2032, R2051 and R2052 to rebuild the missing first key of R1040. The transfers cover 2-3% and give no prose.

Nine more contextual values, each consistent at every occurrence: 741=haar (12x), 39=hun, 2=een, 176^^=mpli (pure et simpliciter), 410^_=zij, 681^_=mogendheden, 724=welgeval, 3^o=stel, 363^o=tusschen. R1036 now at 1,613/1,719 (93.8%).

Read 50 key entries that DECODE's R1038 transcription left illegible or mislabelled directly from the codebook scans (the word stands to the left of its code; parallel homophone columns confirm faint words). 41 were kept after checking them against the R1036 contexts (e.g. 781=geheel, 748''=commercie, 488_=Zijne Keizerlijke Majesteit, 515o=twaalf, 640 barred circle=Russisch). R1036 now at 1,663/1,719 (96.7%). The rest are low-confidence, shadowed or blank in the scans.

Greek-project passage checked group by group against the codebook scans: three earlier scan readings had taken the word to the right of the code (54'' is alhoewel, not alle; 314'' behalven; 941_ observeeren, not obtineeren); 47_ is k, not DECODE's l (gives Griekse and Denemarken); 327=el, 92_=houden, 121=die, 862^^=het, 448''=con fixed by alphabetical place; 644_ reads 'Veld Ma..' (rest in the binding shadow), 339_ faint ('man'?). Not yet applied to decode_1765.py.

Letter images 5416-5417 checked: the '^_' DECODE writes before some groups is a dash after the previous group, so 380 there is plain 380 = van (four DECODE 'krijgen?') and 303 = die (not koop); 21 tokens take their only mark from that dash. The group after 362_ (jong) is an interlinear 191 = ens (DECODE: 19). The first line of image 5417 is cut off in the photograph, losing the end of the Greek sentence.

Normalised Dutch reading of the Emperor/Greek-project passage (tokens 239-466, 686-775) with English, graded M/I: Constantine in the hands of a Greek woman and taught Greek, orders to Field Marshal Ru[man]zow (probably Rumyantsev, unverified) for twelve Greek boys; the Empress silent even to her confidants but the project not dropped. Open: 231o, 77o, 738, 299, 553's role, [dan] (601 with a bar, komen: probably an encoding slip), the lost line.

Greek-project passage: open groups read from their place in the R1038 codebook scans: 738 = grond (M), 299 = favoriet (I), 231^o = verder (I); 77^o ('Stans' in the book) and the line cut off on image 5417 still open.

One-key review (Lasry's rule, 14 Oct 2026): R1040 changes codebook at group 180 of image 5459, so the outcome is given per key in outcome.parts: the Croiset 1765 key (R1036 and the second part of R1040, 5,256 of 5,956 groups given a value, counted from R1040_second_key_tokens.tsv) and the missing Rechteren-family code (first 1,928 groups, not solved). The entry is read in part because R1040 is not read in full.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R1036 and R1040 DECODE transcriptions and the machine decipherments (R1040 second part only; the first part's key is missing); key = parsed R1038 codebook with context values, plus the scan readings

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): R1036_machine_decipherment.txt and R1040_second_key_machine_decipherment.txt read through; words split into letters, bracketed codes and query marks break nearly every sentence (docs/_check_reading.py 0.18 and 0.11 clean). Both relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read; method read after matching with key from external sources -> not solved; fraction_read 0.967 -> 0. The R1038 key match stands.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b19): DECODE R1036 and R1040 re-fetched: one DOC attachment each (DECODE's ciphertext transcriptions, already in the folder); every image opened (R1036 9, R1040 23, main checkout): no interlinear, margin or slip decipherment, no clear copy. Nationaal Archief: 1.01.02 inv. 7408, 3.01.25 inv. 610, 1.02.13 inv. 114 and 158 have no scans online. No edition known.

The 30 Sept 2026 corrections applied in decode_1765.py (R1036_SEPT30): the '^_' DECODE puts after a comma dropped as a mark (a dash after the previous group), key entries re-read on the scans (54^" alhoewel, 314^" behalven, 941^_ observeeren, 47^_ k, 327 el, 92^_ houden, 121 die, 862^^ het, 448^" con, 223^o veele, 743 dat, 853^_ niet, 559 gehad, 80 eeren, 135 barred-circle zoek, 299 favoriet, 231^o verder) and the interlinear group 191 (ens, not 19) added on image 5416; 52^o sedert eenigen and 71^" appuyeeren adopted from the 'high' scan readings (R1038_scan_readings.tsv).

Context pass on R1040 part 2 (b19_kwic.py): 28 values adopted only where they fit every occurrence in R1040 part 2 and R1036 (R1040_B19: 34^_ in, 21^^ of, 78 eenen (W-eenen), 15^_ het hof van, 81^_ honderd, 213^o twee, 922 Hertog, 343^_ me, 341^_ mari, 495^_ mede, 800^_ omstandigheden, 617^" courier, 178 eerst ...; DECODE key misreadings 161 t, 801^" deel, 777^_ niet, 227^" atie, 689 formeeren, 316^" belang); rejected after test: 120, 969^", 940, 851, 690^_, 226, 7^_, 79^o, 761^^, 40^_, 265^_, 5^^, 831^_ (R1040_part2_reread_log.md). Image 5474 found to be in the first, missing code (its marks ^' and ^__, 69% coverage, nonsense after the last words of 5473): the 1765 segment is 5,625 groups.

R1036 and R1040 part 2 normalised group by group into readings with the figures' spelling and DECODE's constant key-transcription letter confusions corrected (R1038_key_misreadings.tsv: hot hof, chi che, cerd eerd, ock ook, hetten hebben ...); every unbracketed word checked as carried (b19_wordcheck.py). Clean-sentence share on the bodies: checker's modern Dutch list 0.09 and 0.038; explicit holes only 0.769 and 0.666. Both set read (grade B); the French quotations of R1040 and the first 2,259 groups stay open.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 2 of 2 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

texts.label: R1036, de Swart to van Bleiswijk, 8 Mar 1782
texts.summary: Johan Isaac de Swart, Dutch resident at St Petersburg, reports to the Grand Pensionary Pieter van Bleiswijk on the French and Spanish answers to the Austro-Russian mediation proposal, Catherine II's Greek project (Grand Duke Constantine taught Greek and given Greek attendants), and Prussia's accession to the Armed Neutrality. Token-level decipherment with the 1765 Croiset key (R1038); 56 groups unread, listed in R1036_unknowns.txt.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b19): the 30 Sept 2026 key and transcription corrections applied in decode_1765.py (the leading dash, 47^_ k, 54^" alhoewel, 191 ens ...), two high scan readings (52^o sedert eenigen, 71^" appuyeeren) and the b19 context values (617^" courier, 341^_ mari, 343^_ me, 316^" belang ...) adopted; DECODE's key-transcription letter confusions normalised where constant (R1038_key_misreadings.tsv); the whole despatch normalised group by group with clear opening and close (R1036_reading.md, every unbracketed word carried, b19_wordcheck.py). Clean-sentence share of the body 0.09 on the checker's modern Dutch list, 0.769 counting explicit holes only (period spelling). Open: 38 groups without a value and the line cut off at the top of image 5417.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 91.1% of the words of R1036_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: R1040, de Swart, 29 Nov 1787 (second part, 1765 key)
texts.summary: De Swart's despatch of 29 November 1787, coded with two codebooks. The 1765-key segment (image 5459 from group 180 to image 5473, 5,625 groups) reports evidence of an Austrian-French alliance, the attention of the Prussian and British representatives at St Petersburg, Kaunitz, the Bavarian exchange and the Duke of Zweibruecken, the German League, the fleet and the Turkish war. The first 1,928 groups and image 5474 (331 groups, 2,259 in all) use a missing Rechteren-family code and are not deciphered.

reading_review.note: Second part read 23 Oct 2026 (b19): context pass on its unread groups (28 values in R1040_B19, each fitting every occurrence here and in R1036), segment corrected to image 5459 group 180 - image 5473 (5,625 groups; 5474 is back in the missing code), normalised reading R1040_part2_reading.md (every unbracketed word carried). Clean-sentence share 0.038 on the checker's modern Dutch list, 0.666 counting explicit holes only; the French quotations read only in part. The first part (2,259 groups) is in a missing code and is not read.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 88.8% of the words of R1040_part2_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.
